title: Smooth base change for the exceptional inverse image
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ u\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ v\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square in which $f$ is
smooth of pure relative dimension
$d$; the
ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not assumed,
the right adjoints $Rf^!$, $Rf'^!$ that occur being, on the coefficients
used here, the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The canonical
comparison

$$
Lu^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^!Lv^*K
$$

is an isomorphism. The morphism $v$ is arbitrary; its base change
$f'$ is smooth of the same relative dimension.

proof.text: Work at the finite stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne p$, as stipulated in the current [def-pur-conventions]. Its finite-coefficient clause makes the constructions here finite-level ones; the integral, rational and algebraically closed versions are separate coefficient transports. Its functor clause specifies separated finite-type $k$-morphisms between finite-type $k$-schemes and refers to [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] for the actual functor and adjunction domains. The latter definition has precisely this standing domain, with $k$ the fixed algebraic closure of the finite field. We use those domains, without taking any preservation or invertibility assertion from the conventions definition. Thus all four schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$ used in that construction for $f$, and use its base change $c'=(j',p')$ for $f'$, as in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. This definition states that $c'$ is a compactification. The compactification comparisons and their compatibility with the Hom bijections in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], clause (3), identify these choices with those in the exceptional functors. Their total spaces are finite type over $k$: the proper part is of finite type, and finite generating sets for two successive algebra extensions generate the composite. Their dimensions therefore have finite bounds by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], as required by [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Clause (1) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] gives that $f'$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. The class-restricted adjunctions in [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge] consequently apply to the coefficients here; no unrestricted pro-etale adjoint datum is being used.

source.place: Opening sentence: establish the finite-coefficient and bounded-class domains before choosing an etale-origin representative.

proof.text: Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$. Since $K$ is bounded constructible, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies $G\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:C_YG\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Ordinary etale inverse images $v_e^*$ and $u_e^*$ are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so they preserve every cohomological lower bound; in particular $v_e^*G$ is bounded below. At finite constant coefficients, [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] computes pro-etale derived pullback termwise by inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] termwise: it gives $C_{Y'}v_e^*G\cong Lv^*C_YG\cong Lv^*K$, naturally in $G$, and gives $Lu^*C_XM\cong C_{X'}u_e^*M$ for every bounded-below etale complex $M$. These comparisons respect the chosen Cartesian square, as stated in that lemma.

source.place: Opening sentence: choose a representative, retaining its isomorphism and its pullbacks.

proof.text:
The natural unit isomorphism $G\xrightarrow{\sim}R
u_{Y,*}C_YG$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], together with $\alpha$, identifies $R
u_{Y,*}K$ with $G$. Put $M=f^	imes G$. The finite formula in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] therefore gives $Rf^!K\cong C_XM$. Put $M'=f'^	imes v_e^*G$. Applying the same defining finite formula to the representative $v_e^*G$ and its unit $v_e^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}R
u_{Y',*}C_{Y'}v_e^*G$ gives $Rf'^!Lv^*K\cong C_{X'}M'$. Clause (2) of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] says that the transported composite $R_c$ preserves bounded-below objects. Hence $C_XM\cong R_cK$ is bounded below. To infer the same for $M$, use [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]: $\mathcal H^i(C_XM)=C_X\mathcal H^i(M)$. Below a lower bound the left side is zero. For the degree-zero sheaf $H=\mathcal H^i(M)$, faithfulness of $C_X$ on $D^+$ implies $1_H=0$, since its image is the identity of the zero object. Thus $H=0$, and $M$ is bounded below. For $M'$, clause (2) applied to $Lv^*K\cong C_{Y'}v_e^*G$ gives a lower bound for $C_{X'}M'$. Exactness gives $\mathcal H^i(C_{X'}M')=C_{X'}\mathcal H^i(M')$; in degrees below that bound, faithfulness on the degree-zero sheaf again gives $1_{\mathcal H^i(M')}=0$. Hence $M'$ is bounded below as well. This verifies the $D^+$ domains rather than attributing preservation by $f^	imes$ itself directly to the statement of the class theorem. Combining these identifications with step 2 gives
$$Lu^*Rf^!K\cong C_{X'}u_e^*f^	imes G,\qquad Rf'^!Lv^*K\cong C_{X'}f'^	imes v_e^*G.$$

source.place: Comparison of actual adjoints with ordinary etale right adjoints; keep all objects in the bounded-below comparison class.

proof.text: Apply [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] to the ordinary etale complex $G$ and the given square. Its hypotheses are met: $A$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$ invertible on all the schemes, $f$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ and has the compactification used above, and $v$ is a morphism of Noetherian schemes. It supplies the specific isomorphism $\beta^e:u_e^*f^\times G\xrightarrow{\sim}f'^\times v_e^*G$, defined as the transpose of $v_e^*\varepsilon^e_G\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_!^e(M))^{-1}$. Denote by $\gamma$ the conjugate of $C_{X'}\beta^e$ under the two identifications of step 3. We next identify $\gamma$ with the canonical comparison in the statement.

source.place: On ordinary derived categories the canonical map is prop-asd-smooth-base-change; retain its counit-transpose characterization.

proof.text:
Let $F_f^e=Rf_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F_f^p=Rf_!^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Denote the natural comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] by $a_f:F_f^pC_X\xrightarrow{\sim}C_YF_f^e$, evaluated on bounded-below etale complexes, and denote the comparison for the base-changed compactification by $a_{f'}:F_{f'}^pC_{X'}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{Y'}F_{f'}^e$. With the identifications of step 3 understood, the pro-etale counit on $K=C_YG$ is
$$\varepsilon^p_K=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\circ a_f(M).$$
Indeed the bounded-class Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] is the etale adjunction transported through the compact-support comparison and the fully faithful $C_T$, as specified in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The identity of $C_Xf^\times G$ corresponds to the identity of $f^\times G$, whose etale transpose is $\varepsilon^e_G$; substituting the comparison $a_f$ gives exactly this formula. For $f'$, the identity of $C_{X'}M'$ corresponds to $1_{M'}$ and then to the etale counit $\varepsilon^{e,f'}_{v_e^*G}$, so $\varepsilon^{p,f'}_{Lv^*K}=C_{Y'}(\varepsilon^{e,f'}_{v_e^*G})\circ a_{f'}(M')$. This is a calculation with the defining adjunction bijections, not an assertion of an adjunction on all pro-etale objects.

source.place: The adjunction bijections and counits transport: write the counit formula by transposing the identity.

proof.text:
Let $t=\operatorname{Ex}_!^p(C_XM):Lv^*F_f^pC_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}^pLu^*C_XM$. The theorem [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] says that this is the transported finite compact-support exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map], and is invertible on the etale-origin bounded-below input $C_XM$. For the proper parts $p,p'$ of the chosen compactifications, [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] identifies the direct-image unit--square--counit exchange with its etale counterpart. Its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses hold because these maps are proper. The compactification formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map] composes that exchange with the specified extension-by-zero identification; [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] states that this whole composite is transported to the pro-etale exchange. Consequently its comparison with the etale compact-support exchange is, after the pullback identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback],
$$a_{f'}(u_e^*M)\circ t=C_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}_!^e(M))\circ Lv^*a_f(M).$$
Substitute this equation and the counit formula of step 5 into the defining transpose of the exceptional comparison:
$$F_{f'}^pLu^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{t^{-1}}Lv^*F_f^pRf^!K\xrightarrow{Lv^*\varepsilon^p_K}Lv^*K.$$
Under $a_{f'}$ this composite is exactly $C_{Y'}\bigl(v_e^*\varepsilon^e_G\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_!^e(M))^{-1}\bigr)$: explicitly, invert the displayed exchange equation to obtain $Lv^*a_f(M)\circ t^{-1}=(C_{Y'}\operatorname{Ex}_!^e(M))^{-1}\circ a_{f'}(u_e^*M)$, and cancel the adjacent comparison isomorphisms. By [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] the resulting etale arrow is the transpose of $\beta^e$. Here its source input $Lu^*Rf^!K\cong C_{X'}u_e^*M$ is bounded below and of etale origin by steps 2-3, and its target $Lv^*K$ is bounded below. The transported adjunction bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] therefore applies and sends both the canonical comparison and $\gamma$ to the very same arrow. Injectivity of that bijection proves equality of the two morphisms. The witness $\alpha$ can be reinserted on both sides by naturality; independence of isomorphic witnesses is part of the cited compact-support and adjunction comparisons.

source.place: Transport of compact-support base change and transposition: prove equality with the specified pro-etale map, not merely an isomorphism of endpoints.

proof.text: A functor carries an inverse pair of arrows to an inverse pair. Thus $C_{X'}\beta^e$ is invertible, and so is its conjugate $\gamma$. Step 6 identifies this conjugate with the canonical comparison, proving the assertion. None of the steps imposes smoothness or properness on $v$; its only restrictions are the standing schemes and coefficient domain. The same computation covers $d=0$, $K=0$, $v$ an identity, and empty source or base, since it uses functors, their natural isomorphisms, and adjunction bijections without choosing a point or a nonempty cover.

source.place: Final sentence: preserve the isomorphism under comparison pullback and conclude for the canonical map.

proof_origin.place: Whole proof: detailed finite-coefficient comparison, with the canonical-map identity proved by counit transposition; current unit sk-prop-cohsm (G12).
